chunks: Muhammad ibn Ismail, from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Ibrahim ibn Umar al-Yamani, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

Verily, Allah created the creation and He knew what they would come to. He commanded them and forbade them. So whatever He commanded them with from anything, He has placed for them the way to abandon it; and they will neither take it nor leave it except by the permission of Allah.

key_terms.آخِذِين: Those who take / act upon (a command)
key_terms.إِذْن: Permission — God's encompassing will or leave within which all things occur
key_terms.السَّبِيل: The way / the path — the real capacity and opportunity granted to each person
key_terms.صَائِرُون: Coming to / destined for — referring to the ultimate outcome or end God foreknew

ai.seo_question: What does Imam al-Sadiq say about divine foreknowledge and human free will in al-Kafi?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (a.s.) articulates the foundational Shia theological position on human agency and divine will, known as 'the matter between two matters' (al-amr bayn al-amrayn). God foreknew human outcomes yet still issued real commands and prohibitions, and for every command He made it genuinely possible for humans to comply or refuse — yet all of this occurs within the encompassing permission of God. This teaching was given in the context of the theological debates of the 2nd century AH, countering both the Jabriyyah (determinists) who denied human agency entirely and the Qadariyyah/Mu'tazila who denied divine sovereignty over human acts.
